title: When and Which Dark Traits Shine? A Multidimensional Review of the Dark Triad in Organizational Research
abstract: ABSTRACT The present research addresses the grand challenge entrenched in the upside of the dark triad (narcissism, Machiavellianism, and psychopathy). To date, reviews have rarely examined the positive aspects of the dark triad. Therefore, this systematic review identifies key mechanisms, contextual conditions, and theoretical frameworks that may leverage the dark triad constructively and mitigate its potentially detrimental manifestations. We summarize the available evidence on the positive side of the dark triad in the domain of organizational behavior using data from 107 studies representing 51,124 respondents. Finally, we review theories used in studying the dark triad and identify significant gaps and trends. We emphasize the necessity of reframing dark triad as potentially context‐dependent, thus expanding the scope of both theory and research methodologies. Reframing the dark triad literature offers an opportunity to advance the field by integrating a range of constructs, theories, and methodologies, which ultimately contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of the dark triad's context‐dependent association with work outcomes.
